title: Elkik equivalence for finite algebras etale away from the completion ideal
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I\subseteq B$ an ideal such that $(B,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $\widehat B=\varprojlim_n B/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Consider the category of commutative $B$-algebras $C$ finite as $B$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]; the morphisms are $B$-algebra homomorphisms. Define the analogous category over $\widehat B$, using the ideal $I\widehat B$. The functor $C\mapsto\widehat B\otimes_B C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is an equivalence of these categories. In particular, every finite $\widehat B$-algebra etale away from $V(I\widehat B)$ is isomorphic, as a $\widehat B$-algebra, to $\widehat B\otimes_B C$ for such a finite $B$-algebra $C$.

source.place: Expose V, Theorem 1.2.4, printed p.64 (Elkik, Solutions d’equations a coefficients dans un anneau henselien, Theoreme 5, as restated there).

proof.text: For every finite $B$-algebra $C$ in the source category, tensoring a finite list of module generators with $\widehat B$ gives generators of $\widehat B\otimes_B C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] to the etale restriction over the complement of $V(I)$; its inverse image is the complement of $V(I\widehat B)$. Thus base change defines the stated functor on objects and algebra homomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] its value is canonically $C^\wedge$. This is an algebra isomorphism: on pure tensors the comparison is $a\otimes c\mapsto a\iota_C(c)$, which preserves units and products, and it is natural in $C$.

Let $C_1,C_2$ be objects of the source category. A finite module generating set also generates the algebra, so each $C_i$ is of finite type over $B$ and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. It is integral over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; hence $(C_2,IC_2)$ is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair]. Apply [lem-per-etale-away-completion-hom-lifting] with $A=B,D=C_1,C=C_2$. Every map $C_1^\wedge\to C_2^\wedge$ lifts uniquely to $C_1\to C_2$. In particular this holds for the $\widehat B$-linear maps in the target category, and the completion of the lift is the given map. Conversely every completed $B$-algebra map is $\widehat B$-linear, as is seen coordinatewise modulo $I^n$. The identifications in Step 1 therefore give bijections on the required Hom sets; the functor is fully faithful.

Let $E$ be an object of the target category. The ring $\widehat B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and is $I$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] applied to $M=B$. Apply [lem-per-completed-etale-jacobian-torsion] over $A=\widehat B$ and ideal $I\widehat B$. This gives a completed polynomial presentation of $E$ whose conormal differential has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a fixed power of $I$, as well as completeness of $E$. The same presentation is over $B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]^\wedge$: [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] gives $B/I^n=\widehat B/I^n\widehat B$, hence the polynomial quotient rings at every level agree. Taking their inverse limits identifies the two completed polynomial rings, their continuous partial derivatives, the kernel ideal $J$, and the displayed conormal differential. Thus its torsion bound is the one needed over $B$.

Apply [lem-per-rig-etale-jacobian-algebraization] to the completed presentation over $B$ from Step 3. It gives a finite type $B$-algebra $D$, etale away from $V(I)$, and a $B$-algebra isomorphism $D^\wedge\cong E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] for the Noetherian ring $D$ (Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]), reduction of this isomorphism gives $D/ID\cong E/IE$. This is finite as a $B/I$-module: reduce module generators for $E$ over $\widehat B$ and use $\widehat B/I\widehat B=B/I$ from Step 3.

Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and of finite type. The whole closed fibre $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}(D/ID)$ is finite over $B/I$ by Step 4, hence proper by [lem-per-affine-proper-finite]. Apply [lem-per-henselian-pair-proper-clopen-lift] with $Y=X_0$. It produces an open and closed $W\subseteq X$, proper over $B$, with $W_0=X_0$. The inclusion $W\to X$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, so is affine by [lem-trf-closed-embedding-affine]; since $X$ is affine, $W$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Write $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$. A morphism between affine schemes is affine by the inverse-image description on basic affine opens. Since $W$ is proper over $B$, [lem-per-affine-proper-finite] shows that $C$ is a finite $B$-module. Over the complement of $V(I)$ the inclusion of $W$ is an open immersion and the structure map of $X$ is etale. Parts (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] therefore show that their composite, the structure map of $W$ there, is etale.

source.place: Tag 0CT9 (lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian), applied to the entire fibre; morphisms.tex Tags 01WN and 04DE.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, every prime of $D$ containing $I^nD$ contains $ID$. Since $W$ contains all of $X_0$, the inverse image of $W$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(D/I^nD)$ is its whole underlying space. As $W\to X$ is an open immersion with restricted structure sheaf, this inverse image is the whole scheme. Thus restriction gives compatible ring isomorphisms $D/I^nD\cong C/I^nC$. Their inverse limit identifies $D^\wedge\cong C^\wedge$ as $B$-algebras. Step 1 identifies $C^\wedge$ with $\widehat B\otimes_B C$; the composite with Step 4 gives the desired isomorphism to $E$. All these maps are $\widehat B$-linear: modulo $I^n$ their scalar action is through $B/I^n$, and equality in the inverse limit is coordinatewise. This proves essential surjectivity. Together with Step 2 it yields the equivalence: choose a representative $C$ and such an isomorphism for each $E$, and lift morphisms by the Hom bijections; uniqueness enforces identities and composition. The stated particular conclusion is the object assertion just established.

The item statement is unchanged and matches ILO V Thm 1.2.4 (p.64): a Noetherian henselian pair, finite algebras étale away from V(I), and an equivalence with finite B̂-algebras. Each new node matches its exact source. (1) lem-per-affine-proper-finite is Stacks 01WN and an exact Mathlib leaf, IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_isAffineHom at Proper.lean:98. The existing nodes give only finite ⇒ proper or a field base. (2) completed-etale-jacobian-torsion combines 0AJP, 0ALQ(1), 0AJU(3) and 00MA(3). (3) rig-etale-jacobian-algebraization is 0AKG(8) with 0AJU(3); A is not assumed complete, as in the source. (4) etale-away-completion-hom-lifting is 0AKJ with the henselization C^h equal to C. (5) henselian-pair-proper-clopen-lift is 0CT9 verbatim. No DAG or blueprint node states any of them; I swept the tags, Elkik, rig-étale and the conormal-torsion and sbc completion nodes. Small cases (I=0, E=A/I, Y=∅, x²=t versus x²=1+t over k[t]_(t)^h) are all consistent. Steps: (1) base change plus the natural c_C, which is multiplicative. (2) C₂ is Noetherian, integral, hence henselian, so the hom-lifting node applies and the functor is fully faithful. (3) B̂/I^n = B/I^n, so the completed presentation over B̂ is literally the same one over B. (4) Algebraization gives D of finite type, and module-completion gives D/ID ≅ E/IE, finite over B/I. (5) The 0CT9 lift of the whole finite closed fibre, then closed-embedding-affine and the 01WN leaf, make W = Spec C finite and étale over U. (6) Since W contains V(ID), D/I^n ≅ C/I^n, which gives essential surjectivity. No hypothesis is missing and nothing comes from SGA. I accept the generic off-unit tool_uses (sk-thm-p1 commutative-algebra and scheme tools, plus lem-trf-closed-embedding-affine).
